reviews.title: Waste of time
reviews.text: App makes you go through the whole set up process, has you make an account, gets all your info and then tells you it is not free.

reviews.title: Broken
reviews.text: App has been crashing on launch for about a week straight. Unusable in its current state.

reviews.title: Did love it, now I have to pay?
reviews.text: I have been using this app for two years, raving and sending multiple people to this app to track calories and other health information. I has been great, but today I log on and now I have to pay for everything that was once free. This is crazy. Fix it or most of us will leave.

reviews.title: Wish I had bought lifetime
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for months and I loved it! Has so many excellent features that make tracking a breeze. However they recently switched over to annual subscriptions, locking me out of many of the features I was using before. If there had been transparency on the switch, I would’ve bought lifetime before. Now on to finding another tracking app =(

reviews.text: This is outrageous how they can charge you for something and I can’t even use the app every time I open it just crashes. I reinstalled it crashes. Yet I paid for the whole year and I can’t even use it.

reviews.title: Useless
reviews.text: I have a lifetime membership that no longer syncs with my Fitbit. I DO NOT want to spend more time every day adding my every step and exercise into another app. Will no longer be using this app.  Why do these designers feel the need to update themselves right out of customers?

reviews.title: Lost feature
reviews.text: Took a break from tracking calories due to some health issues. Started tracking again and was disappointed to see that scanning a barcode was taken away and is only available in the paid version. It can be time-consuming already as it is to track calories so something like this makes it more difficult. Please bring back this feature to the free version.

reviews.title: Paid Content Ruined It
reviews.text: Nothing much more to say: the titles self explanatory. It’s shocking how they keep finding more features to lock behind a paywall. It used to be my favorite app to keep track of my food, now it’s no longer as good as it used to be. Don’t get greedy, you lose customers that way.

reviews.title: Greedy developers
reviews.text:
I liked the app for its simplicity and its subscription offerings but it seems like lately businesses never can get enough money from their current customers.

The developers have now added an additional charge for the Lab analysis of the nutrition patterns even if you paid for a lifetime subscription.

It should have been included with ALL subscriptions, but especially for those of us who committed to a lifetime supporter.

Whatever happened to company gratitude by grandfathering in those who helped make a company successful?

I guess commitment only goes one way when it comes to business

I definitely won’t be recommending this app anymore

reviews.title: This app has turned into a money grab
reviews.text: This app is nothing but a money grab. The simple act of scanning a food label has become a premium feature. I am a long time user of this app but I’m afraid i’ve had to look elsewhere and mfp is so much better. I can scan food without having to pay, I can schedule what I will eat without paying. Premium features are supposed to be premium and make the experience better. It’s not supposed to make basic features unavailable. You might as well charge to download the app itself if this is how it is. Don’t even bother with this app.

reviews.title: Salt info very poor
reviews.text: The app is quite helpful to a point, but even after speaking with support, their inaction to include salt content rather than sodium for uk is disappointing to the point of useless. The ai scanner will not scan salt content on uk labels and many items already registered have inaccurate salt content or lack it entirely. Salt is such a major component to the health of your being, with high blood pressure affecting 1.4 billion globally. In the uk, 1 in 3 adults are affected with high blood pressure and it acts as a primary cause of heart attacks, strokes and kidney failure. I don’t want updated graphics. I want correctly and easy to use salt content.

reviews.title: Only 7 days free trial

The app is subscription based. As in, you need a subscription to use it at all.
This is not communicated when you first join. They take you through a long onboarding process and only at the end you are told that there you need to pay. 
Waste of time.

reviews.title: DISAPPOINTED!!! Greedy Changes
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app consistently since 2023. I took a break for a couple months from calorie tracking as I was only maintaining my weight but I would continue to update my weight in app. However, I recently opened the app back up for calorie tracking purposes only to discover that several features that I heavily relied on are suddenly placed behind a paywall. I’m really frustrated with this outcome as a college student who always struggled to manage my health as well as the stress of being a student. The app was the only thing that made it easy by allowing me to scan barcodes of food items I’ve purchased as well as view my overall macros for the day. I understand that the app needs to make money but there are various premium features that made sense to pay extra for previously and this did not need to be taken away from loyal users. Now, the bare essentials for the app are inaccessible and I’m incredibly disappointed. I dislike any app that makes the free tier nearly useless. I’m hoping for this to be reversed but it is highly unlikely. The yearly rate for this membership is 80 dollars which is incredibly ridiculous and greedy. Although there is currently a sale I don’t see these “updates” as reasonable personally. I understand this may be worth it for some people but as someone who felt blindsided by the switch I don’t know how to justify a purchase like this. I’ve fortunately seen other people agree with me. Do better.

reviews.title: Bad new changes
reviews.text: Used to be a great little app, now demanding I fill out a lengthy survey to use it, despite having paid for it the whole time. No option to skip it, no “it’s none of your business option”, just endless questions and a pointless new graphical design I have to learn. What a huge disappointment, have to assume the original devs got bought out by some faceless PE firm

reviews.title: App Developers Don’t Listen To Community
reviews.text: I’ve been a power user for a few years, logging every day for my body building. I even had premium for a long time before the developers removed lots of features I used. I’ve also been active on the loseitapp Reddit community which is filled with people the same as me who have seen this app get worse and worse with every update, never listening to its user-base. I migrated from MyFitnessPal to LoseIT but I have no other option than to move away from loseit completely. It’s a shall of what it was before and unfortunately there’s just much better apps out there now for this. I’m migrating over to MacroFactor who seem to actually be able to employ actual decent UX/UI developers who care and listen to what their userbase want. I won’t be looking back at all… good riddens.

reviews.title: Ruined with the new UI changes
reviews.text: Has been great, and have been using it as a paying customer for the last two years. But the recent UI changes make it so frustrating to use. Information density is way worse in searches, and the daily log view is much less helpful now. I think the fundamental issue is a misunderstanding of how people use the app - it is not a lifestyle app I am going to use for hours per day, I just want to open, log, and get on with my life. The new changes are making this worse.

reviews.title: Becoming useless
reviews.text: I’ve used this app for a few years and it was really easy to use and I preferred it over other tracking apps. Mainly I’ve just been tracking my daily calories and it was good to see at the top of the log how I was doing for the week. Over time more and more features have been hidden behind a paywall and I now can’t even see my weekly calories unless I go to the dashboard because it only shows my daily calories on the log. Also there seems to be an advert every other time I open the app. I thought as I use this app everyday and have done for a few years I would bite the bullet and pay to unlock all the features until I saw it was £75 for the year when like others have said it used to be £15. I will now look at finding an alternative app where I can get sufficient basic features at no extra cost.
